curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students record themselves reading aloud, practicing appropriate pacing, intonation, and expression. Focus: Enhancing oral reading expression and rate. Examples: Reading a dialogue between characters, reading an enthusiastic informative paragraph, reading a short poem, reading an empathetic narrative, reading a persuasive sentence, reading a list of exclamatory remarks. Constraints: Use audio analysis in the read-aloud-studio to compare against a model reading.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested
learnerAction: Reread a short expressive text (dialogue, exclamations, a question) with pacing and expression after hearing a model.

components.title: Read Like the Characters
components.intent: Grade 2 dialogue between two characters with real end punctuation: at least one ?, one ! and one statement; feelings stated in the story.

components.title: Mark the Pauses, Then Read
components.intent: Grade 2 short connected passage about something exciting (not about reading or recording). Lines carry commas, ! and ? the child can use for phrasing.

evidenceCriteria: Word accuracy on the reread after the model (scored).

Expression, pacing and intonation are coached only. "There is no prosody response class, so nothing grades how it sounded" (ReadAloudStudio.tsx:29-38). Mastery of expression needs an adult listening: external review protocol.
coverageLimits: expression draw: lines were about the objective's own words ("Clear intonation sounds so good.").
dialogue draw: no line had end punctuation.
No comparison to the model reading exists; reads are judged against the print.

recommendation.rationale: Repair content (RAS-1 meta-topic, RAS-3 missing punctuation). Do not build prosody scoring: the project rules out judging live audio quality, so expression remains coached practice with an external check.
